{{Short description|Series of two mathematics textbooks}}
{{italic title}}
'''''Calculus''''' is a two-volume textbook series by mathematician [[Tom M. Apostol]].

==History==

Apostol wrote the two-volume ''Calculus'' set because there was no existing textbook suitable for the students entering [[Caltech]] in the late 1950s. Over the course of a year, the mathematics faculty debated how to restructure their introductory classes, eventually developing a revised plan that would coordinate with the [[physics]] classes being taught at the same time. Having already published one book (''Mathematical Analysis'' in 1957<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bartle |first=Robert G. |date=1957 |title=none |journal=Pi Mu Epsilon Journal |volume=2 |issue=7 |pages=324–325 |issn=0031-952X |jstor=24345109}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mears |first=F. M. |date=1958 |title=none |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=65 |issue=6 |pages=463–464 |doi=10.2307/2310749 |jstor=2310749}}</ref>), Apostol found himself "eager" to write the lecture notes. Originally distributed as [[mimeograph]]ed booklets, these notes became the ''Calculus'' volumes. Students at Caltech referred to them as "Tommy 1" and "Tommy 2".<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Donald J. |last1=Albers |first2=Tom |last2=Apostol |title=An Interview with Tom Apostol |journal=The College Mathematics Journal |volume=28 |number=4 |date=September 1997 |pages=250–270 |doi=10.1080/07468342.1997.11973873 |jstor=2687147}}</ref>

The first volume, on single-variable [[integral calculus|integral]] and [[differential calculus]], was the first book printed by the Blaisdell Publishing Company,<ref name="Cunningham1"/> a publisher in [[Waltham, Massachusetts]], acquired by [[Ginn and Company]] in 1963.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://research.hrc.utexas.edu/watch/fob_search_results_next.cfm?FOBFirmName=C&FOBNote=&locSTARTROW=41 |title=Firms Out of Business |website=[[Harry Ransom Center]] |access-date=2025-10-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Altbach |first1=Philip G. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=o-IjCQAAQBAJ&dq=%22blaisdell+publishing%22&pg=PA239 |title=International Book Publishing: An Encyclopedia |last2=Hoshino |first2=Edith S. |date=2015-05-08 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-134-26126-0 |pages=239 |language=en}}</ref>

Volume 1 was published in 1961,<ref name="Cunningham1" /> and volume 2 the year after.<ref name=":0" /> A second edition of Volume 1 was published in 1967,<ref name=":1" /><ref name="MAA1" /> incorporating two new chapters on [[linear algebra]].<ref>{{cite journal|first=R. A. |last=Rankin |title=none |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |volume=53 |number=384 |date=May 1969 |pages=218 |doi=10.2307/3614609 |jstor=3614609 }}</ref> Volume 2 received a second edition in 1969.<ref name="MAA2" />

==Contents==
The first volume covers integration before teaching differentiation, swapping the typical order in which the subjects are presented.<ref name="Cunningham1" /><ref name=":2" /> After introducing the integrals and derivatives, the two basic operations of calculus, it covers elementary [[transcendental function]]s, the basics of [[differential equation]]s, and other topics including [[analytic geometry]], [[infinite series]] and the mathematics of [[planet]]ary [[orbit]]s.<ref name="Cunningham1" />

Volume 2 covers [[multivariable calculus]], including topics in [[vector calculus]] like [[Green's theorem]] and [[Stokes' theorem]], as well as [[linear differential equation]]s and the theory of [[probability]].<ref name=":0" />

==Reception==

F. Cunningham Jr., reviewing the first volume for ''[[The American Mathematical Monthly]],'' praised the quality of its exposition and the exercises that Apostol included. Cunningham wrote that he himself "would favor even more emphasis on applications, and a lighter touch on some questions of rigor".<ref name="Cunningham1">{{cite journal|title=none <!--deliberately done this way because the title in the metadata is just one of those long strings of boilerplate that includes the publisher and the long-obsolete price --> |first=F. Jr. |last=Cunningham |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=69 |number=5 |date=May 1962 |pages=449–451 |doi=10.2307/2312166 |jstor=2312166}}</ref> Of the second volume, he declared that it "if anything surpasses the first in excellence of workmanship, and occasions for detailed criticism are not worth mentioning".<ref name=":0">{{cite journal|title=none <!-- deliberate, as above --> |first=F. Jr. |last=Cunningham |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=70 |number=5 |date=May 1963 |pages=587–588 |doi=10.2307/2312105 |jstor=2312105}}</ref>

In ''[[The Mathematical Gazette]],'' R. L. Goodstein called the first volume "beautifully produced". He offered what he considered minor criticisms, like the "old-fashioned" way in which the book treated [[partial fraction]]s.<ref name=":2">{{cite journal|first=R. L. |last=Goodstein |title=none <!-- again deliberate --> |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |volume=46 |number=358 |date=December 1962 |pages=333–334 |jstor=3611796}}</ref>

E. D. Bolker called the second edition an improvement upon the first, describing it as "easier to use in the classroom and no less stimulating". Bolker considered it suitable for an advanced first-year university course, and declared, "All instructors should own a copy to use as a reference work."<ref name=":1">{{cite journal|first=E. D. |last=Bolker |title=none |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=77 |number=1  |date=January 1970 |pages=88–89 |doi=10.2307/2316878 |jstor=2316878}}</ref>

Both volumes have been deemed "essential for undergraduate mathematics libraries" by the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name="MAA1">{{cite web |url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/calculus-calculus-volume-1-one-variable-calculus-with-an-introduction-to-linear-algebra |title=Calculus, Volume 1: One-Variable Calculus with an Introduction to Linear Algebra |website=MAA Reviews |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=2025-10-26}}</ref><ref name="MAA2">{{cite web|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/calculus-volume-2-multi-variable-calculus-and-linear-algebra-with-applications |title=Calculus, Volume 2: Multi-Variable Calculus and Linear Algebra with Applications |website=MAA Reviews |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=2025-10-26}}</ref>
